speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual symptom. Have you noticed any specific triggers for these episodes, such as flashing lights, loud noises, or a particular smell? Also, do you ever experience déjà vu or an unsettling feeling right before they happen?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Complex Partial Seizure (Temporal Lobe Epilepsy).

Based on your description of an "unsettling feeling," a "muddy taste" (gustatory aura), and post-ictal confusion, this clinical picture is highly characteristic of a focal seizure originating in the temporal lobe. While I am confident in this assessment, I would normally request an MRI of the brain and an EEG to confirm the diagnosis and rule out structural causes.
